records.assetReview: Position origin x=320 at 60 px/m gives endpoints x=200 and x=440 for −2 and +2 m. Three distinct instants show rest at the right endpoint and two separate passages through equilibrium. Each velocity arrow is 120 px at 20 px/(m/s), giving oriented velocities ±6 m/s. Phase graph origin (100,900), 200/π px/rad and 20 px/(m/s): the −6 sinθ curve has minimum (200,1020), zero (300,900), maximum (400,780) and final zero (500,900). All 241 samples, complete XML and full native image were read. Positive bars 240 and 160 px at 40 px/(m/s) give 6 and 4 m/s, ratio 2/3. Effective markers on each separate arrow were checked.
records.distractors: 12 uses the full endpoint separation 2 A instead of amplitude A; 3 copies angular frequency. Maximum modulus occurs at equilibrium, while the oriented velocity reaches both +6 and −6 m/s.
records.manualArithmetic: Differentiate displacement: v=−Aω sin(ωt+φ). Maximum sine modulus one gives speed maximum 2 m times 3 s⁻¹, or 6 m/s.
records.physicalAssumptions: A material point follows ideal harmonic displacement in an inertial frame, positive constant amplitude and angular frequency within each trial, arbitrary constant initial phase, no damping. The requested maximum is a positive modulus, with both oriented velocity signs during each cycle. This is material motion, not wave-shape propagation. Cross-trial amplitude-frequency constraints have explicit dimensioned coefficients; display is continuous and dimensionless.
